row.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- uh, كهربجي، هو مهندس، uh, مهندس.
row.why: Saying who the man he called is - 'he is not a kahrabji, he is an engineer' - is a present noun predicate: Levantine negates it with مش and no 'to be' (C4); ما يكون is neither that nor a licensed ykoon context (B8: only after lamma/iza or for habits). The man's job is a present fact, so ما كان (r2) is not the target either. She said nothing about it; her 10:30 صلح لي moves to his next clause.
row.english: He isn't an electrician, he's an engineer.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the slip; the transcript supports C4 (noun predicate negated with a verb form) over B6 (the identity claim is present, not past); B8 goes in bucket2 for the stray ykoon.

row.why: Explaining why he stayed home today (اليوم ضليت بي بيتي): 'because there is AC' - existence in the plain present is في / عندي, not يكون (B8: ykoon only after lamma/iza or for habits; C1: no 'to be' in the present). She moved on to شو بتتذكر at 13:04 without a fix. 'air conditioning' is not on her sheet, so the English word itself is not an error. B reading.
row.english: because there is air conditioning (at home)

rulings.why: Real let-pass: عشان يكون AC is not how a native states that the AC is there; kept as grammar-B, low because his intent (cause vs purpose) is not spelled out.

row.why: 'One word': the modifier وحدة sits after the noun like an adjective; he put it first (English order) and she recast noun-first, بس كلمة وحدة. A7 is the rule broken (modifier after the noun); E1 is the secondary tag because the modifier is the number one.

rulings.why: Both readers agree on the slip; the transcript shows a word-order fix, which is A7's rule (E1 only covers the form of the noun after 2 / 3-10 / 11+), so A7 with E1 as bucket2.

His production is transcribed only as the tail زري and she said she did not hear the t, i.e. the person marker was missing; he fixed to بتكسري at 33:31. Low: the transcript holds only a fragment, so whether he said بكسري (B18) or كسري (B1) cannot be shown.

row.why: Conjugating انكسر for هو/هي he produced بينكسري (masc بي- prefix + fem -ي ending), a form that exists for no subject; she did not fix it, she redirected him to the skipped إنتو. Low: he was switching subjects mid-word. Her هو at 45:38 fixes a different slip (هي بينكسر).

row.why: إحنا of the un-verb انكسر is بننكسر (b-n-nkasir); he gave بنكسر, which is the إحنا form of plain كسر ('we break'), and she went straight into usage talk (46:08). Low: ASR may have collapsed the double ن, and her 45:57 line (transcribed بتنكسر) may itself have been her feeding him بننكسر.

rulings.why: Kept as a low-confidence let-pass: the transcript shows بنكسر after a hesitation, but a merged double ن in ASR is plausible, so the merger should weigh it lightly.
